Labels and decoding SDMX data

Source: vignettes/labels-and-decoding.Rmd
labels-and-decoding.Rmd

Why keep codes and add labels?

SDMX uses stable dimension codes in series keys. People analysing the results often prefer readable descriptions. tuiksdmx can add Turkish and/or English labels from the DSD-referenced Codelists without overwriting the original code columns. That matters for reproducibility, joins and future queries. Labels describe defined codes; they do not establish that a code has observations for every period.

This article follows the CPI Dataflow DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01, as tested during development. Live structures, translations and returned observations may change. All examples are intentionally not executed when this vignette is built. Set TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY securely (for example, in your personal .Renviron) or supply api_key = api to authenticated calls.

library(tuiksdmx)
id <- "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01"
profile <- tuik_flow_profile(id)

1. Start with raw codes

Use a short observation window for a first example, but remember that a bounded request with no filters still retrieves all series in that window. A period bound is not a maximum row count.

raw <- tuik_get_data(
  profile,
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01"
)

# The original coded dimension values are preserved
raw[, intersect(c("FREQ", "DEGISIM", "COICOP_2018", "TIME_PERIOD", "OBS_VALUE"),
                names(raw)), drop = FALSE]

2. Add Turkish, English or both labels at retrieval time

labels has four permitted values: "none" (default), "tr", "en", "both". For a focused example, use label_dimensions to decode only the needed dimensions; leaving it NULL requests labels for all coded dimensions present in the returned data.

cpi_tr <- tuik_get_data(
  profile,
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01",
  labels = "tr",
  label_dimensions = c("FREQ", "DEGISIM")
)

# The code column and its Turkish label appear side by side
head(cpi_tr[, c("DEGISIM", "DEGISIM_label_tr"), drop = FALSE])

cpi_both <- tuik_get_data(
  profile,
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01",
  labels = "both",
  label_dimensions = c("DEGISIM", "COICOP_2018")
)

head(cpi_both[, c("DEGISIM", "DEGISIM_label_tr", "DEGISIM_label_en"),
              drop = FALSE])

Each new name takes the form DIMENSION_label_tr or DIMENSION_label_en. For example, COICOP_2018_label_tr accompanies COICOP_2018; TIME_PERIOD and OBS_VALUE are not Codelist label columns. Labels are additional columns, not replacements for the SDMX keys.

3. Decode data you have already downloaded

You do not have to repeat observation retrieval merely to change the label language. tuik_decode_data() accepts an existing data frame and the corresponding profile:

decoded <- tuik_decode_data(
  raw,
  profile,
  dimensions = c("FREQ", "DEGISIM"),
  language = "both"
)

head(decoded[, c("FREQ", "FREQ_label_tr", "FREQ_label_en"),
             drop = FALSE])

The function matches observation codes against Codelist definitions and preserves the existing observations and their row count. It may still need metadata requests to fetch Codelists; decoding an existing table avoids re-downloading observations, not necessarily every network call.

4. Choose dimensions from metadata, not guesswork

Inspect the Dataflow’s key dimensions and code domain before requesting labels:

tuik_filter_dimensions(profile)
tuik_dimension_codes(profile, dimension = "DEGISIM")

# Inspect codes/descriptions in the interactive-style helper
tuik_explore(profile, dimension = "COICOP_2018", search = "gıda")

Not every structural component refers to a Codelist. dimensions in tuik_decode_data() and label_dimensions in tuik_get_data() must name coded dimensions actually present in the data. Specifying an unknown or uncoded dimension results in an error rather than a fabricated description.

5. Labels do not prove availability

A label comes from a theoretical Codelist domain. It is not evidence that a code has data for January 2026 or for a chosen filter combination.

# Defined domain: Codelist codes and descriptions
possible <- tuik_dimension_codes(profile, dimension = "COICOP_2018")

# Observed domain: codes in returned observation rows for a bounded query
observed <- tuik_available_codes(
  profile,
  dimension = "COICOP_2018",
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01",
  allow_all = TRUE
)

The observed query above explicitly authorizes an all download. It may be costly even with one month selected. tuik_available_codes() reports codes observed in the retrieved rows; it does not fetch SDMX ContentConstraint metadata.

6. Common pitfalls

  • labels = "none" together with label_dimensions = ... is invalid: ask for "tr", "en" or "both" first.
  • Unknown translations can yield NA label values; they do not alter the original SDMX codes.
  • Do not convert dimension code columns to numeric before decoding. Codes are identifiers and may contain leading zeros or nonnumeric symbols.
  • Calling tuik_decode_data() again for the same dimensions/language on an already decoded table can raise a name-collision error. Decode from raw or select new, nonconflicting label columns.
  • Labels do not reduce response size. Use a complete DSD key when you need more selective server-side retrieval, as described in Filtering, SDMX keys and performance.
